changelog: Rewrote severity clause of C5 to distinguish splits inside multi-character nominal modifiers (worst) from short/locally-headed modifiers or cuts immediately after the modifier (milder); addresses the primary finding about preferring later cuts that keep modifier+head together.
findings: When two candidate cuts fall inside the same nominal modifier, the prompt sometimes prefers an earlier internal split; the measured targets prefer the later cut that preserves the modifier+head span.
The prompt allows cuts that split numerals from their immediately following unit/date/measure, breaking single referents and causing high contradiction/cohesion loss.

diagnosis.why: Rewriting C5 changed the model’s severity signal so its top-ranked cuts shifted (rank_depth shows clear gains at depths 1–2) but cuts deeper in the list became less faithful (depths 3–5 drop). Concretely the model began proposing earlier/high-ranked splits that separate punctuation/quotes and sometimes cut inside multi-character nominal modifiers (the worst examples), which produced a small net harm concentrated in long-latency bins even though the very top positions improved.
diagnosis.lesson: Keep the severity wording from signaling that internal characters of multi-character nominals are acceptable cut points—preserve modifier+head integrity for deeper-ranked cuts while only adjusting how immediately-post-modifier cuts are scored.
